chunks: Hadith 2141 — Whoever recites the Talbiyah seventy times during his ihram with faith and sincere seeking of reward, Allah makes a thousand angels bear witness for him to freedom from the Fire and freedom from hypocrisy.

Whoever reaches the Haram, halts, performs ghusl, takes his sandals in his hand, then enters the Haram barefoot out of humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah erases one hundred thousand sins from him, records one hundred thousand good deeds for him, builds for him one hundred thousand degrees, and fulfills for him one hundred thousand needs.
Whoever enters Makkah with tranquility and dignity, Allah forgives his sin; that is, that he enters it without being arrogant or domineering.
Whoever enters the mosque barefoot with tranquility, dignity, and humility, Allah forgives him.
Whoever looks at the Ka'bah recognizing its due right, Allah forgives his sins and suffices him regarding what concerns him.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: the state of consecration for hajj in which specific rites and restrictions apply
key_terms.النِّفَاقِ: hypocrisy, from which the person is granted freedom

ai.seo_question: What rewards are mentioned for Talbiyah, entering the Haram humbly, and looking at the Ka'bah in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the great rewards for acts of devotion and humility during hajj, especially Talbiyah, entering the Haram and Makkah with sakinah and waqar, and looking at the Ka'bah with recognition of its right. It emphasizes that sincere worship joined with humility and freedom from arrogance becomes a means of forgiveness, elevation in rank, and protection from the Fire and nifaq.
